content.text: You're a digital creator in Zimbabwe, Nigeria, Ghana, or Pakistan, and you're tired of Stripe's restrictions and high fees. You've tried to sell your ebooks, courses, and software on various platforms, but they've always been met with payment rejections or forced to accept payment through a third-party service that takes a huge cut of your earnings. It's time to take back control of your digital store and deploy a sovereign commerce infrastructure that works for you, not against you. You've come across COREMERCH, a sovereign commerce infrastructure company that's been pressure-tested against actual payment rejection, currency collapse, and financial isolation. With COREMERCH, you can deploy a digital store on Cloudflare Pages for free, configure automatic crypto payment processing with NOWPayments, and ensure instant product delivery using Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Your goal is to deploy a Stack 01 or Stack 02 solution that meets your needs and scales with your business. Let's dive in.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

Cloudflare Pages offers a free hosting solution that's perfect for digital creators who want to deploy a digital store without worrying about high fees or platform restrictions. With Cloudflare Pages, you can host your digital products and configure your payment and delivery pipeline using Cloudflare Workers and NOWPayments. The Edge Commerce Stack ($197) is a premium solution that offers end-to-end testing, 30-day support, and 5 loaded products. However, with the Sovereign Starter Stack ($97), you can deploy a Stack 01 solution in 4-6 hours, following the Sovereign Blueprint, and configure automatic crypto payment processing with NOWPayments. This infrastructure works when platforms fail because it's built on free and open-source tools, giving you full control over your data and payments. You can deploy a Stack 01 solution for free, configure your payment and delivery pipeline, and scale your business using the Edge Commerce Stack. The question is, which solution is right for you? Let's explore the steps to deploy a Stack 01 solution and then discuss the benefits of the Edge Commerce Stack.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before you deploy a Stack 01 solution, you need to have a few things in place. First, you need to create a Cloudflare account and set up a new project. You'll also need to create a new GitHub repository for your digital products. Next, you'll need to configure your payment and delivery pipeline using NOWPayments and Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Finally, you'll need to create a new Google Apps Script project to handle backend logic and integrate with NOWPayments. With these tools and services in place, you're ready to deploy your Stack 01 solution in 4-6 hours, following the Sovereign Blueprint. Don't worry if you're not familiar with these tools – the Sovereign Blueprint provides a step-by-step guide to deploying a Stack 01 solution for free.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Configuring your payment and delivery pipeline is a critical step in deploying a Stack 01 solution. With NOWPayments, you can configure automatic crypto payment processing, and with Google Drive or Cloudflare R2, you can ensure instant product delivery. You'll need to create a new NOWPayments account and configure your payment options, including setting up a new cryptocurrency wallet and configuring your payment notifications. Next, you'll need to create a new Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 account and configure your delivery options, including setting up a new bucket and configuring your delivery notifications. With these services in place, you're ready to deploy your payment and delivery pipeline and start selling your digital products.

Next, you'll need to configure your delivery options, including setting up a new bucket and configuring your delivery notifications. With these steps in place, you're ready to go live and process your first transaction. Once your Stack 01 solution is up and running, it's time to scale your business and deploy more digital products.
